bottles.name: Aia Vecchia Sor Ugo Bolgheri Superiore
bottles.profile: Ripe dark cherry, plum and blueberry with menthol, rosemary, licorice and a hint of chocolate and incense. Full-bodied and round with plenty of dusty tannin and ripe acidity — a polished coastal Tuscan Super Tuscan in the Bordeaux mould.
bottles.tenSecond: The Super Tuscan — coastal Tuscan Cabernet-Merlot with dark cherry, herbs and dusty tannin, the Italian answer to a Napa or Bordeaux red.
bottles.pairWhy: Full body and firm dusty tannin are built for red meat — they cut the fat of ribeye and lamb — while the menthol-herb lift keeps the rich wine from tasting heavy.

pronunciation.say: Aia Vecchia Sor Ugo Bolgheri Superiore
pronunciation.respell: AH-yah VEK-kyah sor OO-goh bol-GHEH-ree soo-peh-ree-OH-reh

bottles.mnemonic: Bolgheri = coastal Tuscany's Bordeaux; Sor Ugo = polished Super Tuscan.
bottles.producerStory: The Pellegrini family grew grapes in Bolgheri for generations, selling fruit to the area's famous estates before founding Aia Vecchia in 1995, named after an old farm building on their land. Sor Ugo is their flagship — a Bordeaux-style blend first developed with noted enologist Tibor Gál and launched in 2001, named for Ugo, the first Pellegrini to work with vines a century ago ('Sor' is an old honorific for Signor).
bottles.whyWePourIt: Our Super Tuscan slot: coastal Bolgheri's ripe, cedar-and-dark-fruit power for the steak-and-statement-red guest, without trophy-label pricing.

bottles.name: Algre Valgañón
bottles.profile: Violet and geranium florals with pink peppercorn and bright red and black fruit. From one of Rioja's highest, coldest villages, it's fresh, gentle and medium-bodied — an elegant, lighter Rioja rather than a heavy oaked Reserva.
bottles.tenSecond: The fresh, floral Rioja — bright red fruit and pink pepper from a cold mountain village, gentler than a big oaky Rioja.
bottles.pairWhy: High acidity and gentle tannin make it food-flexible: it lifts tomato and cured meats and complements roast chicken and lamb sausage without the weight of an oak-heavy red.
bottles.mnemonic: Alegre y Valgañón = the growers' names; high cold Rioja village = fresh, floral.
bottles.producerStory: Husband-and-wife team Óscar Alegre and Eva Valgañón, who met studying enology in Italy, have made wine since 2014 in Fonzaleche — a village of about 80 people that is one of the highest, coldest corners of far-western Rioja Alta. They farm small old parcels in Fonzaleche and nearby Sajazarra, often ferment with stems, and use only neutral French oak — deliberately the opposite of big, oaky commercial Rioja.
bottles.whyWePourIt: The Rioja that surprises people who think they know Rioja — floral, fresh and gentle, our high-altitude answer to a Burgundy-drinker's red.

bottles.name: Alta Mora Etna Rosso
bottles.profile: Pale ruby with red cherry, cranberry, dried rose, and pepper over a faint iron-and-salt mineral thread. Bright acidity and fine, delicate tannins — an elegant, savory Etna red.
bottles.tenSecond: Sicily's Pinot Noir — grown high on Mount Etna's volcano, so it's pale, fresh, and red-fruited, not heavy.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and fine, gentle tannin mean it slips alongside lighter meats, mushrooms, and tomato without overpowering; the savory mineral streak loves umami.

pronunciation.respell: AHL-tah MOH-rah, ET-nah ROH-soh, neh-REL-loh mahs-kah-LEH-zeh

bottles.mnemonic: Alta Mora = 'high' on Etna; altitude + volcano = pale, high-acid, Pinot-shaped red.
bottles.producerStory: Alta Mora — 'high and black,' for Etna's altitude and dark volcanic soils — is the Sicilian Cusumano brothers' Mount Etna project, begun in 2013 when they bought their first vineyard contrade on the volcano's north slope and rebuilt the traditional dry-stone terraces. The grapes are estate-grown, hand-harvested Nerello Mascalese from some of Europe's highest vineyards, including very old vines in Contrada Guardiola.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Our volcanic light red — the 'Sicilian Pinot Noir' for the elegant-red drinker who wants something savoury, mineral and a little exotic.

bottles.name: Bideona Cabezadas
bottles.profile: Stone fruit and white flowers with a subtle struck-match mineral note. Light and crisp on the palate, refreshingly dry with a slightly mineral finish — from old hilltop vines on calcareous clay.
bottles.tenSecond: A crisp, dry white Rioja from old Viura vines — stone fruit and minerals, with a little texture; a refreshing left-field pick.
bottles.pairWhy: High acidity and a clean dry finish refresh the palate against fried and oily plates, while the gentle texture and orchard-fruit weight let it sit comfortably next to vegetable and cheese small plates.
bottles.mnemonic: Cabezadas = hilltop 'headlands'; old vines up high give it cut.
bottles.producerStory: Bideona is a village-and-vineyard-focused winery in Villabuena de Álava, Rioja Alavesa, backed by Basque txakoli producer Gorka Izagirre and run by the Península Vinicultores team. It farms over 300 tiny old parcels — average age around 50 years — across the villages of Rioja Alavesa. 'Cabezadas' are the high tops of those vineyards where white vines were traditionally planted, and this is an unoaked, mostly-Viura field blend from them.
bottles.whyWePourIt: A crisp, stony old-vine white at our friendliest bottle price — the insider's alternative when a guest asks for 'just a dry white'.

bottles.name: Brandini Langhe Filari Corti
bottles.profile: Perfumed rose, violet and red cherry with classic licorice and tar on the finish. High acid and firm but silky tannins make it elegant rather than heavy — the gateway Nebbiolo.
bottles.tenSecond: The classy Italian red — rose and red cherry with grippy tannin and bright acid, made for truffle, mushroom and rich pasta.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and firm tannin cut through fat and umami: the acid refreshes against duck and mushroom, the tannin grips meaty richness without overwhelming the wine's perfume.
bottles.mnemonic: Nebbiolo = nebbia = fog; pale colour, big perfume, firm grip.
bottles.producerStory: Agricola Brandini is a roughly 25-hectare estate in the high-altitude zones of La Morra, in Barolo country, run by young sisters Serena and Giovanna Bagnasco and certified organic since 2011. Filari Corti is their Langhe Nebbiolo: picked earlier than their Barolo fruit and aged in large oak, so it leads with bright red fruit, roses and silky La Morra tannins.
bottles.whyWePourIt: The gateway Nebbiolo — Barolo-country perfume and structure at a third of Barolo money, perfect with charcuterie or anything truffled.

bottles.name: Castello di Potentino Sacromonte
bottles.profile: Brambly red and black berry, garden herbs and sweet blossom over a stony, mineral core, with nervy raspy tannins and a tangy finish. A fresher, higher-altitude take on Sangiovese than Chianti.
bottles.tenSecond: A mineral, mountain-grown Sangiovese — fresh sour-cherry acid and herbs, the brainier cousin of the house Chianti.
bottles.pairWhy: High acidity is built for tomato and herb dishes — it matches the acid in the sauce so the wine stays lively — while medium tannin handles cured meats and grilled lamb.
bottles.mnemonic: Sacromonte = 'sacred mountain' (Monte Amiata) — volcanic, high, fresh.
bottles.producerStory: Castello di Potentino is an ancient castle estate on the slopes of Monte Amiata, Tuscany's extinct volcano, restored and run by English winemaker Charlotte Horton, who has made wine in Tuscany for over two decades. She ferments with native yeasts and minimal intervention; Sacromonte, her 100% Sangiovese, is named for the 'sacred mountain' the Etruscans believed was home of the gods.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Sangiovese with a story — a castle, a volcano and an Englishwoman — pouring fresher and more mineral than Chianti for the curious red drinker.

bottles.name: Castello di Verduno Alba
bottles.profile: Vivid blackberry, sour cherry, and plum with violet and a little dark spice. Barbera's signature high acid with low tannin makes it juicy, fresh, and easy-drinking.
bottles.tenSecond: Piedmont Barbera — all juicy dark cherry and zip, with almost no tannin. The crowd-pleasing red from Barolo country.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and low tannin cut through tomato, fat, and salt without any grip to fight the food — the natural partner for pizza, pasta, and sausage.
bottles.mnemonic: Barbera = high acid, low tannin = the juicy Italian pizza-and-pasta red from Barolo's backyard.
bottles.producerStory: Castello di Verduno is run from a 16th-century castle in Verduno, in Barolo country, owned by the Burlotto family since 1909 — the same family behind the famed G.B. Burlotto estate next door. Today Gabriella Burlotto and Franco Bianco run it with their daughters and longtime winemaker Mario Andrion, farming about 10 hectares split between Verduno and Barbaresco; the Barbera comes from a tiny old parcel planted in the 1950s and '60s.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Juicy, high-acid, low-tannin Piedmont red from a storied Barolo-family castle — our most food-flexible Italian pour.

bottles.name: Charlotte & Jean Baptiste Senat Amalgame
bottles.grape: Grenache Noir, Grenache Gris & old Languedoc varieties (Piquepoul, Counoise, Terret)
bottles.profile: Bright, floral, and almost rose-pale — red berries, garrigue herbs, and a cool, juicy lift. Barely any tannin; built for chilling and easy drinking.
bottles.tenSecond: A pale, floral light red from the South of France — chill it slightly; it drinks like the easiest red on the list.
bottles.pairWhy: Light body and low tannin mean it never fights delicate or spiced food; fresh acid and herbal lift refresh fat and salt without weighing the plate down.
bottles.mnemonic: 'Amalgame' = a co-fermented field blend led by Grenache; pale, floral, gulpable.
bottles.producerStory: Charlotte and Jean-Baptiste Sénat left Paris in 1995 for Jean-Baptiste's family land in Trausse, in the Minervois hills of the Languedoc, and became pioneers of natural winemaking there — organic farming, native varieties, no fining or filtration. Amalgame is their pale, gluggable cuvée: old southern varieties (Grenache noir and gris with Piquepoul, Counoise and Terret) co-fermented whole-cluster and bottled young.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Our chillable natural red — barely-there tannin and garrigue-scented red fruit for patio season and the orange-wine crowd.

bottles.name: Christophe Mignon ADN de Meunier Brut Nature
bottles.profile: A 100% Pinot Meunier grower Champagne with zero dosage, so it is bone-dry and laser-focused. Red-fruit and faint floral nose; the palate is savoury and mineral — citrus confit, chamomile, dried herbs, graphite and white pepper — full-ish for a Champagne with taut, high acidity and a salty, super-dry finish.
bottles.tenSecond: Real grower Champagne, all Pinot Meunier, zero sugar — bone-dry, mineral, and savoury for the bubbles purist.
bottles.pairWhy: Bone-dry, high-acid Champagne with a fine, persistent mousse is the ultimate palate-scrubber for brine and fat, and the savoury, mineral Meunier weight lets it carry richer plates too — so it shines from raw oysters to fried snacks and creamy cheese.

pronunciation.say: Christophe Mignon ADN de Meunier Brut Nature
pronunciation.respell: krees-TOFF mee-NYOHN ah-deh-EN deh muh-NYAY broot nah-TEWR

bottles.mnemonic: ADN = French for DNA — this is the 'DNA of Meunier', all one grape, nothing added (zero dosage).
bottles.producerStory: Christophe Mignon is a fifth-generation grower in Festigny and Le Breuil in the Vallée de la Marne, farming about 6.5 hectares that are roughly 90% Pinot Meunier — vines his great-grandparents planted. He farms by biodynamic principles and the lunar calendar, and ADN de Meunier is his calling card: 100% Meunier, long lees aging, and zero dosage, so it finishes bone-dry.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Our grower-Champagne statement — proof that humble Meunier, in obsessive hands, can be laser-focused and savoury rather than simply fruity.

bottles.name: Château Larose Perganson
bottles.profile: Blackcurrant and red plum with cedar, tobacco, graphite and a touch of bell pepper. Medium-to-full bodied with firm, structured tannins — a classic, savoury left-bank Bordeaux built around Cabernet and Merlot.
bottles.tenSecond: The textbook Bordeaux — cassis, cedar and tobacco with firm tannin, the classic steak-and-lamb claret.
bottles.pairWhy: Firm Cabernet tannin is made for red meat: it binds with protein and fat so steak tastes smoother and the wine softens — the original reason claret and beef are paired.
aliases: chateau larose perganson cru bourgeois superieur
bottles.mnemonic: Haut-Médoc = left-bank Bordeaux = Cabernet-led, cedar and cassis.
bottles.producerStory: Larose Perganson's origins trace to 1719, when Jean-Pierre de Pontet founded the estate in the Haut-Médoc; today it is part of Vignobles de Larose and made in the cellars of its larger neighbour, Château Larose-Trintaudon, near Saint-Laurent-du-Médoc. It carries Cru Bourgeois Supérieur status and is a classic Cabernet-Merlot left-bank claret in the cedar-and-blackcurrant mould.
bottles.whyWePourIt: The classic Bordeaux slot — savoury, structured left-bank claret with real age-worthiness for the traditionalist at the table.

bottles.name: Cirelli Frizzante Bianco
bottles.profile: Pale straw with a soft, fine frizzante fizz. Lemon, green apple and a touch of peach with herbal/floral lift, lively acidity and a clean, dry, lightly mineral finish. Lighter and gentler than Champagne — a relaxed, low-alcohol (~10.5%) sparkler.
bottles.tenSecond: Dry organic Italian bubbles — light, citrusy, and easy; my low-key aperitivo and seafood-starter pour.
bottles.pairWhy: Light body and high acid with a gentle fizz refresh the palate without overpowering delicate food — so it lifts briny seafood, fried snacks and creamy cheese instead of competing with them.
bottles.mnemonic: Frizzante = lightly fizzy — a gentle, easy bubble, softer than full Champagne sparkle.
bottles.producerStory: Francesco Cirelli founded his 22-hectare certified-organic farm near Atri, in Abruzzo's Teramo hills a few kilometres from the Adriatic, in 2003 — a true mixed farm with olives, figs, wheat, geese and pigs alongside the vines, best known for fermenting in terracotta amphorae. The Frizzante Bianco is his easy-going side: Trebbiano with a gentle natural sparkle, spontaneously fermented and low in alcohol.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Our relaxed aperitif fizz — softer and friendlier than Champagne, low-alcohol, and a natural fit for sessions that start before dinner.

bottles.name: Ciro Picariello Bru Emm
bottles.profile: Green apple, lemon zest, white flowers, and citrus over a strong mineral, saline core. Dry, crisp, and long — fresh thanks to the inland, ~400m vineyards near Benevento.
bottles.tenSecond: Southern-Italian Falanghina that drinks crisp and mineral — apple, lemon, and salt, made for seafood.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and a saline, mineral finish slice through olive oil and fried batter and lift briny shellfish, while the medium body keeps up with lightly roasted white meats without flattening them.
bottles.mnemonic: Bru-Emm = Bruno + Emma, his kids; bright and zesty like the name sounds.
bottles.producerStory: Ciro Picariello is one of Campania's most respected white-wine growers, famous above all for Fiano di Avellino from high-altitude vineyards around Summonte and Montefredane; he and his wife founded the estate in 1997. BruEmm — named for the youngest family generation, Bruno and Emma — is his Falanghina, from a vineyard he farms near Benevento at around 400 metres, aged briefly in stainless steel to keep it fresh.
bottles.whyWePourIt: A southern-Italian crisp white with a saline snap — the off-the-beaten-path alternative to Pinot Grigio from a cult Fiano producer.

bottles.name: Claire Naudin Mallon
bottles.profile: Lemon and orchard stone fruit with a savory, slightly herbal edge. Dry and high-acid with more texture than typical Aligoté thanks to lees aging — low-intervention Burgundy from the Hautes-Côtes.
bottles.tenSecond: Burgundy's other white grape — crisp, citrusy Aligoté with a savory twist; like Chardonnay's leaner, zippier cousin.
bottles.pairWhy: Bright acidity and a savory streak handle herb, allium, and tangy dishes the way a Chablis would, while the extra texture lets it stand up to creamier or cheesy small plates without going heavy.
bottles.mnemonic: Mallon = the artist who paints the label each year; arty, savory Aligoté.
bottles.producerStory: Claire Naudin runs her family's Domaine Henri Naudin-Ferrand in Magny-lès-Villers, in the Hautes-Côtes above Burgundy's Côte d'Or, which she took over from her father in 1994. She is one of Burgundy's most outspoken champions of the underdog Aligoté grape, working with minimal intervention and very low sulfur; Mallon is her textured, lees-aged Bourgogne Aligoté.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Insider Burgundy — the sommelier's grape from a cult low-intervention grower, scratching the white-Burgundy itch without white-Burgundy pricing.

bottles.name: Clos Bellane Valréas
bottles.region: Côtes du Rhône Villages Valréas, Rhône Valley
bottles.profile: A southern-Rhône white led by Marsanne with Viognier lift — white peach, citrus, white flowers and honeysuckle over a stony, mineral finish. The 400m limestone altitude keeps an otherwise sunny site fresh and balanced rather than heavy.
bottles.tenSecond: A floral, gently full white from the high slopes of the southern Rhône — peach and white flowers with real freshness. Lovely with roast chicken, halibut, and creamy plates.
bottles.pairWhy: Medium body and a round, aromatic mouthfeel match richer vegetable and poultry dishes, while the altitude-driven freshness keeps it from feeling flat against fat or spice.
bottles.mnemonic: Bellane on the high 'plateau' = altitude = a Rhône white that stays fresh.
bottles.producerStory: Clos Bellane is a single high-altitude estate in the hills above Valréas, at the cool northern edge of the southern Rhône, bought in 2010 by winemaker Stéphane Vedeau with the goal of making fresher styles of Côtes du Rhône Villages. The vineyards sit at roughly 400 metres on limestone and were converted to certified organic farming; whites come from Marsanne, Roussanne and Viognier.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Our richer-but-still-fresh Rhône white — peachy and floral with a stony finish, the step between crisp whites and full Chardonnay.

bottles.name: Cusumano Lucido
bottles.profile: Straw-gold with ripe pineapple, banana, and candied-citrus aromas. Dry and rounded on the palate with good freshness — the 'Lucido' clone of Catarratto keeps more acidity than the everyday version.
bottles.tenSecond: A sunny, easy Sicilian white — ripe citrus and pineapple, dry and fresh, and the friendly price on the crisp-white lane.
bottles.pairWhy: Medium acidity and a fruity, rounded body make it an easy match for herby Mediterranean and lightly fried plates — enough freshness to cut oil without the bracing edge that can clash with milder dishes.
bottles.mnemonic: Lucido = 'shiny' grape skins = bright, sunny Sicilian white.
bottles.producerStory: Cusumano was founded in 2001 by brothers Diego and Alberto Cusumano in Partinico, west of Palermo, and has grown into one of Sicily's leading estates with vineyards across the island. Lucido is the local name for the finer clone of Catarratto, western Sicily's historic white grape — this bottling keeps it bright, unoaked and sunny.
bottles.whyWePourIt: The easy Sicilian opener — ripe, friendly and our most accessible white, an honest by-the-bottle value for groups.

bottles.name: Denizot Sancerre
bottles.profile: Grapefruit, lime, gooseberry, and a chalky, flinty snap from Sancerre's limestone soils. Bone-dry and tightly focused with a long mineral finish.
bottles.tenSecond: The benchmark crisp white — flinty Loire Sauvignon Blanc, bone-dry and built for oysters and goat cheese.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and zero sweetness cut through brine, fat, and fried batter, while the citrus echoes lemon-dressed seafood and greens — it refreshes the palate instead of competing with delicate plates.
bottles.mnemonic: Sancerre = flint = the matchstick-crisp Sauvignon Blanc.
bottles.producerStory: Domaine Denizot is an eight-generation family estate in Verdigny, in the heart of Sancerre, today led by Thibauld Denizot with his parents Chantal and Christian. They farm about 19 hectares — three-quarters Sauvignon Blanc — mostly on the prized limestone 'caillottes' soils around Amigny and Chavignol, with minimal intervention in the cellar.
bottles.whyWePourIt: The benchmark crisp white — flinty, bone-dry Sancerre that needs no explanation and flatters oysters, martinis and people-watching alike.

bottles.name: Domaine Breton Pierres Rousses
bottles.profile: Quince, ripe pear, honeysuckle and a touch of flint, with barrel-aging adding a creamy, lightly waxy texture over a high-acid Loire spine. Dry and fresh despite the round mouthfeel.
bottles.tenSecond: A grown-up dry Chenin from Vouvray — orchard fruit and texture from the barrel, but a crisp Loire backbone that loves chicken, trout, and creamy dishes.
bottles.pairWhy: High acidity cuts cream and richness while the barrel-built texture matches weightier plates, so it bridges from seafood to roast chicken without losing freshness.
bottles.mnemonic: Pierres Rousses = 'red stones' = flinty Vouvray soil = stony, dry Chenin.
bottles.producerStory: Catherine and Pierre Breton are pioneers of the Loire's natural-wine movement, farming organically/biodynamically in Bourgueil since the 1980s, with family vines in Catherine's native Vouvray. Pierres Rousses comes from roughly 55-year-old Chenin Blanc on flinty clay ('pierres rousses') soils, fermented and aged in used barrels to a dry, textured style — a cuvée associated with the next generation, their son Paul, who focuses on the whites.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Grown-up dry Chenin — waxy texture and quince over Loire acidity, our pick for guests who want a white with grip and a natural-wine pedigree.

bottles.name: Domaine Buisson-Charles Meursault Vieilles Vignes
bottles.profile: Classic Meursault from six old-vine parcels — ripe white stone fruit, sweet lemon, hazelnut and a creamy, mouth-filling body, all carried on a firm mineral line and good acid. Aged in barrel (around 20% new oak) then rested in tank, so it's rich but elegant, never blowsy.
bottles.tenSecond: This is the special-occasion white Burgundy — a rich, creamy, mineral old-vine Meursault. If a table wants the benchmark buttery-but-elegant Chardonnay, this is it.
bottles.pairWhy: Full body and creamy texture mirror butter, cream and shellfish, while the mineral acid line keeps a rich dish lifted — built for shellfish, roast chicken, and cream sauces.

pronunciation.respell: doh-MEN bwee-SOHN SHARL mur-SOH vee-AY VEEN-yuh

bottles.mnemonic: Meursault = the rich, creamy heartland of white Burgundy; Vieilles Vignes = old vines = concentration.
bottles.producerStory: Domaine Buisson-Charles is a small family estate in Meursault dating back over a century, now run by Patrick Essa — son-in-law of third-generation vigneron Michel Buisson — with his wife Catherine. From about 6 hectares, Essa has pushed the domaine into Meursault's top rank; the Vieilles Vignes comes from old parcels (vines of roughly 60 to 100 years) and is raised in barrel with restrained new oak for a rich-but-chiselled style.
bottles.whyWePourIt: The celebration white — true old-vine Meursault with hazelnut and cream over a mineral spine, for the table that wants the best Chardonnay in the house.

bottles.name: Domaine Gour de Chaulé Gigondas Les Jardinières
bottles.profile: Ripe and macerated red fruit, garrigue herbs, lavender and crushed white pepper with a minty lift. Full-bodied and suave, with dusty but supple old-vine tannins and good length — generous southern Rhône with structure.
bottles.tenSecond: The warm, generous southern-Rhône red — ripe red fruit, garrigue and spice with full body and supple grip, made for lamb and steak.
bottles.pairWhy: Ripe fruit, herb (garrigue) and full body mirror Provençal-style grilled meats; supple tannin handles the fat of lamb and ribeye while the wine stays generous rather than austere.

pronunciation.say: Domaine Gour de Chaulé Gigondas Les Jardinières
pronunciation.respell: doh-MEN goor duh shoh-LAY zhee-gon-DAHSS lay zhar-dee-NYAIR

bottles.mnemonic: Gigondas = Châteauneuf's rugged neighbour; Grenache-led, full and warm.
bottles.producerStory: Domaine du Gour de Chaulé was founded in 1900 by Eugène Bonfils in the heart of Gigondas village and has been passed down largely through the family's women — today fourth-generation Stéphanie Fumoso runs it, joined by her son Paul in 2018. Its 10 hectares of old vines across many small parcels are raised traditionally in concrete tanks and old foudres; Les Jardinières is a Grenache-led blend with Syrah and Mourvèdre.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Our plush southern-Rhône GSM — old-vine Gigondas warmth, garrigue and supple tannin for the guest who wants generosity without jamminess.

bottles.name: Domaine de Colette Coteaux de Colette
bottles.profile: Juicy, crunchy red fruit — cherry, raspberry, red currant — with floral lift and a wet-stone freshness. Silky low tannin and bright acid make it the breeziest red on the list.
bottles.tenSecond: Old-vine Beaujolais Gamay — bright, juicy cherry with barely any tannin. Chill it slightly; it's everybody's easy red.
bottles.pairWhy: Low tannin and high acid mean it never clashes — it refreshes salt, fat, and charcuterie, and is light enough for poultry, salmon, and lighter plates.

pronunciation.say: Domaine de Colette Coteaux de Colette
pronunciation.respell: doh-MEN deh koh-LET, koh-TOH deh koh-LET

bottles.mnemonic: Gamay from Beaujolais = Pinot's juicy, low-tannin cousin; chillable and crowd-pleasing.
bottles.producerStory: Domaine de Colette is a 16-hectare family estate in Lantignié, on the edge of Beaujolais' Régnié and Morgon crus, officially created in 1953 by René Gauthier and run today by his son Jacky with his wife Evelyne. The Gamay vines grow on pink granite with an average age around 55 years (some over 80), hand-harvested and farmed organically (in conversion since 2020).
bottles.whyWePourIt: The breeziest red on the list — old-vine cru-country Gamay that takes a light chill and bridges rosé drinkers into red territory.

bottles.name: Domaine de la Rochette Mâcon-Bussières Mont Sard
bottles.profile: White Burgundy from old vines on the stony slopes of Mont Sard — oatmeal and cream, ripe apple and a light nutty edge from time on lees, with pithy dry acidity and some real concentration. Generous and ripe without feeling oaky or over-ripe.
bottles.tenSecond: Proper white Burgundy at a friendly price — creamy and ripe-apple-textured from barrel and lees, but with stony grip. The crowd-pleasing Chardonnay for chicken, cod, and creamy pasta.
bottles.pairWhy: Lees-built texture and medium body wrap around butter, cream and roasted flavours, while the pithy dry acidity stops it turning heavy — a natural match for richer fish and poultry.

pronunciation.say: Domaine de la Rochette Mâcon-Bussières Mont Sard
pronunciation.respell: doh-MEN duh lah roh-SHET MAH-kohn boo-see-AIR mohn SAHR

bottles.mnemonic: Mont Sard = the stony 'mont' (hill) = stony, mineral Mâcon Chardonnay.
bottles.producerStory: Domaine de la Rochette farms about 10 hectares in Bussières and Milly-Lamartine in the Mâconnais, and since 2015 has been part-owned and made by Frédéric-Marc Burrier of Maison Joseph Burrier — the family behind Château de Beauregard in Pouilly-Fuissé. The Mont Sard cuvée comes from a parcel of vines on the steep, stony marly-limestone slopes beneath Mont Sard itself, giving unusually concentrated Mâcon Chardonnay.
bottles.whyWePourIt: White Burgundy flavour at Mâcon money — creamy, nutty old-vine Chardonnay that overdelivers for its place on the list.

bottles.name: Donnhoff Feinherb
bottles.profile: White peach, lemon, spring flowers, and crunchy slate. Gently off-dry ('feinherb') with a silky texture and bright, piquant acidity that keeps it tasting fresh rather than sweet.
bottles.tenSecond: A barely-off-dry German Riesling — peach and lemon with a slate tingle; the high acid makes it taste fresh, not sweet, and it tames spice.
bottles.pairWhy: The whisper of sweetness cushions chili heat and salt while the high acidity keeps it lifted, so it calms spicy and aromatic plates that would fight a bone-dry wine.
bottles.mnemonic: Feinherb = 'fine-tart' = a little sweet, kept honest by tart acidity.
bottles.producerStory: The Dönnhoff family has farmed in Oberhausen on the Nahe river for over 250 years, and under Helmut Dönnhoff — and now his son Cornelius, winemaker since 2007 — the estate became one of Germany's most acclaimed Riesling producers, a member of the VDP with about 25 hectares of top sites. Wines are pressed quickly after picking and fermented in traditional casks and steel for purity.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Our barely-off-dry Riesling from a legendary grower — the trace of sweetness makes it the list's best friend for spice, heat and salt.

bottles.name: Eleonore Moreau Petit Chablis
bottles.profile: Unoaked Chablis Chardonnay — green apple, lemon and white flowers with a flinty, oyster-shell minerality and a steely, high-acid finish. Aged unusually long on the lees in tank, so it carries a little more texture and depth than a typical Petit Chablis.
bottles.tenSecond: Steely, citrusy Chablis Chardonnay — no oak, all freshness and stony minerality. My textbook oyster-and-seafood white that's a step up from the by-the-glass crisp whites.
bottles.pairWhy: High acidity and a saline, flinty edge sharpen oysters and raw seafood and cut through fried and creamy bites, while the lees-aging adds just enough body for lighter cooked fish.
bottles.mnemonic: Chablis soil is full of fossil oyster shells — so Chablis is the oyster wine.
bottles.producerStory: Eléonore Moreau farms her family's 13 hectares in Poilly-sur-Serein, at the southeastern edge of the Chablis appellation, under the label Domaine des Pérégrins — vines her father planted in the early 1980s on land the family has held for generations. She returned in 2011, took over winemaking in 2016, pushed through organic certification, and ages her Petit Chablis unusually long on the lees in tank for extra texture.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Oyster-shell Chablis character from a small organic grower — steely, flinty and a sharp-value alternative to bigger-name Chablis.

bottles.name: Fletcher Barbaresco Recta Pete
bottles.profile: Bright red cherry, rose petal and dried herb over tar, iron and roasted chestnut, with firm dusty tannins and a long amaro finish. Elegant and perfumed — Barbaresco's classier, slightly softer take on Nebbiolo.
bottles.tenSecond: The serious Nebbiolo splurge — Barbaresco perfume of cherry, rose and tar with firm tannin built for truffle, duck and lamb.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and firm tannin demand fat and umami: they scrub richness from duck and lamb and resonate with earthy mushroom and truffle, while the wine's perfume survives bold dishes.
bottles.mnemonic: Fletcher = 'shoot straight'; Barbaresco = Barolo's elegant sibling.
bottles.producerStory: Dave Fletcher is an Adelaide-trained Australian who moved to Piedmont in 2007 to work for the famed Ceretto estate, rising to a senior winemaking role there before building his own label inside Barbaresco's converted old train station. Recta Pete — 'shoot straight' in his family's Scots dialect — is his classic-style Barbaresco, blending fruit from top crus, fermented with native yeasts and aged about two years in old oak, bottled unfiltered.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Barbaresco's perfume and polish with a great story — the outsider-made-good bottle for the guest choosing between elegance and power.

bottles.name: Griesel Blanc de Noirs
bottles.profile: A white sparkling made from red grapes (Pinot Noir & Meunier), traditional-method with 20+ months on the lees. Brioche, white bread crust, ripe pear, apple and walnut with a whisper of red fruit; powerful yet crisp, fine mousse, mineral salinity and a dry, racy Brut finish.
bottles.tenSecond: Germany's answer to grower Champagne — Pinot Noir and Meunier, traditional-method, crisp and brioche-y. The serious-bubbles bottle.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and a fine, scrubbing mousse cut through salt and fat, while the lees-driven brioche weight and medium body give it enough presence to stand up to richer plates — so it works from oysters to fried chicken and creamy cheese.
bottles.mnemonic: Blanc de Noirs = 'white from blacks' — white wine pressed pale from red Pinot grapes.
bottles.producerStory: Griesel & Compagnie was founded in 2013 in Bensheim as the first dedicated sparkling-wine house on Germany's tiny Hessische Bergstraße, working out of a historic 1904 estate with a vaulted cellar. Cellar master Niko Brandner — a former banker who retrained in viticulture — quickly pushed Griesel into the top tier of German Sekt, making traditional-method (bottle-fermented) wines with a minimum of about 20 months on the lees. The Blanc de Noirs is white sparkling pressed from the red Champagne grapes Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It's the serious grower-Champagne experience at a friendlier price — the bottle for guests who want real traditional-method bubbles with a story they haven't heard before.

bottles.name: Gulfi Nerojbleo
bottles.profile: Ripe blackberry and plum, crushed violet, lavender and spice over a savoury, mineral underlay. Full-bodied with muscular but fine tannins — a brighter, more structured Nero d'Avola from higher-elevation Sicilian (Hyblean Mountains) sites.
bottles.tenSecond: The big, dark Sicilian red — blackberry, violet and spice with real body and grip, made for lamb, sausage and ribeye.
bottles.pairWhy: Full body and firm tannin stand up to fatty, smoky meats, while the savoury herbal-mineral streak keeps it from tasting jammy alongside grilled lamb and sausage.
bottles.mnemonic: Nero d'Avola = 'black of Avola'; Sicily's dark, full-bodied red.
bottles.producerStory: Gulfi is a family estate just north of Chiaramonte Gulfi in southeastern Sicily, founded by Vito Catania and now run by his son Matteo, farming around 70 hectares of native Sicilian varieties organically. They were pioneers of single-vineyard Nero d'Avola, and Nerojbleo is their benchmark bottling — 100% Nero d'Avola from older vines on the hilly, calcareous-marl sites of the Hyblaean hills, aged about 12 months in barrique. The higher-elevation fruit gives a fresher, more structured take on Sicily's signature dark grape.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It fills the big-Sicilian-red slot with grip and savour instead of jam — the structured warm-climate Italian that flatters lamb and ribeye without tasting like a fruit bomb.

bottles.name: Kistler
bottles.region: Russian River Valley, Sonoma County, California, USA
bottles.profile: Ripe black cherry, raspberry and violet layered with clove, cola and forest floor. Plush and seamless on the palate but kept lively by bright acidity and velvety tannin — the splurge Pinot.
bottles.tenSecond: The special-occasion California Pinot — silky black cherry and spice, elegant enough for duck, salmon and mushrooms.
bottles.pairWhy: Medium body and supple tannin slot under lighter proteins, while the bright acidity lifts fatty fish and rich poultry without overpowering — Pinot's classic crowd-pleasing middle ground.
bottles.mnemonic: Kistler — famous for Chardonnay, here a plush splurge Pinot.
bottles.producerStory: Kistler Vineyards was founded in 1978 by Steve Kistler and Mark Bixler in Sonoma County, and built its cult reputation on single-vineyard, single-clone Chardonnay before adding Pinot Noir from the same exacting playbook. Based in the Russian River Valley since 1992, the winery works a handful of cool Sonoma sites, with its Pinot program built on heritage vine selections of Burgundian origin. Winemaker Jason Kesner has led the cellar since Steve Kistler's 2017 retirement, keeping the house style plush, precise and site-driven.
bottles.whyWePourIt: This is the splurge Pinot — a California cult name guests recognize, giving the list a true special-occasion light red between Burgundy and the steak Cabs.

bottles.name: Landron Muscadet-Sevre et Maine Amphibolite
bottles.profile: Lemon, lime, green apple, and sea-spray salinity over a soft mineral edge from iron-rich amphibolite rock. Bone-dry, lean, and zippy with a saline finish — aged on fine lees for a touch of texture.
bottles.tenSecond: The oyster wine — bone-dry, salty, lemony Muscadet from old sea-floor rock. Lean, mineral, and made for the sea.
bottles.pairWhy: Light body and searing acidity won't overpower delicate raw seafood, and the natural salinity mirrors brine — it's the textbook structural match for oysters and crudo.

pronunciation.respell: lahn-DROHN moos-kah-DEH SEV-ruh ay MEN am-fee-boh-LEET

bottles.mnemonic: Amphibolite = sea-floor rock = salty, sea-bright wine.
bottles.producerStory: Jo Landron took over his family's domaine near Nantes in 1990 and grew it to about 50 hectares of Melon de Bourgogne, converting to certified organic farming in 2002 and certified biodynamics in 2011 — he's one of Muscadet's reference growers. Amphibolite is named for the greenish metamorphic sea-floor rock under this single 7.5-hectare parcel; it's hand-harvested, fermented with natural yeasts and aged briefly on fine lees in concrete to stay lean, citrusy and saline. It's made to be drunk young, as the purest expression of that rock.
bottles.whyWePourIt: Every raw-bar list needs the textbook oyster wine, and this is it — bone-dry, salty, organic Muscadet from a benchmark grower at a gentle price.

bottles.name: Malahierba Vinos Maleza
bottles.profile: High-toned cherry, pomegranate, and cranberry with wild herbs, sweet spice, and a tangy, savory finish. Thin-skinned Rufete gives soft, velvety tannins and bright, lifted acidity — think Pinot's lighter cousin.
bottles.tenSecond: A rare mountain grape from western Spain — light, red-fruited, and zippy, like a wilder Pinot Noir. Pour it for the Burgundy curious.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and feather-light tannin keep it nimble; it lifts herbs, vinaigrette, and lighter proteins instead of flattening them, and the acid scrubs fat clean.
bottles.mnemonic: Rufete = thin-skinned mountain grape = pale, high-acid, soft-tannin — Spain's answer to Pinot.
bottles.producerStory: Malahierba is a tiny project started in the late 2010s (first vintage 2019) by agricultural engineers Silvia Rocher and Manuel García in the Sierra de Salamanca, the wild mountain country of western Spain near Portugal. They rescue heritage parcels of the local Rufete grape — many vines 80 to 120 years old, never treated with herbicides — working only about 5 hectares in total. Maleza is a single high-altitude granite parcel near San Esteban de la Sierra, gently extracted and aged in acacia, with production measured in hundreds of bottles in some vintages.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It's the insider's light red — a rare old-vine mountain grape with Pinot-like brightness that gives the Burgundy-curious guest a genuine discovery.

bottles.name: Maloof Where Ya Pjs At?
bottles.profile: An orange wine: skin-contact Pinot Gris brings soft herbs, dried apricot and a light cherry-candy note with a gentle savory grip, lifted by high-toned acidity, with barrel-fermented Riesling in the blend. Dry, unfined and unfiltered.
bottles.tenSecond: This is our orange wine — skin-contact Pinot Gris from Oregon. A little grippy and savory, super dry, and a brilliant bridge between white and red for charcuterie and grilled dishes.
bottles.pairWhy: Skin-contact gives a light tannic grip and savory texture that stands up to spice, fat and char, while the high acid keeps it refreshing — so it handles dishes a normal white can't.
bottles.mnemonic: PJs = cozy, casual, fun = the easygoing orange wine.
bottles.producerStory: Maloof Wines is run by Ross and Bee Maloof — he came out of a decade in Philadelphia restaurants, she from aerospace materials engineering — at their vineyard and winery near Forest Grove in the northwest Willamette Valley, certified organic since 2020. They specialize in aromatic grapes underrepresented in Oregon, especially Pinot Gris and Riesling. Where Ya PJs At? is their playful orange wine: Pinot Gris fermented dry on its skins (around three weeks), blended with barrel-fermented Riesling, and bottled unfined and unfiltered.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It's the list's orange-wine moment — savory, grippy and fun, bridging white and red for charcuterie and grilled plates while signalling we take natural wine seriously without being precious about it.

bottles.name: Mount Eden Wolff Vineyard
bottles.profile: A Burgundian-style California Chardonnay from old vines in the cool Edna Valley — honeysuckle, ripe citrus and stone fruit with a fresh-baked-bread note, barrel-fermented in French oak and aged about 8 months. Stony, soil-driven and energetic, with bright, penetrating acidity rather than butter and vanilla.
bottles.tenSecond: California Chardonnay that drinks like white Burgundy — barrel-built texture but high acid and stony freshness, from the coolest valley in the state. The serious crossover white.
bottles.pairWhy: High acidity and a tight mineral core keep the wine fresh against richer fish and creamy plates, while gentle barrel texture gives just enough weight to match them — Burgundian poise without heavy oak.
bottles.mnemonic: Mount Eden makes Burgundy-minded Chardonnay; Wolff = cool Edna Valley fruit = freshness over fat.
bottles.producerStory: Mount Eden Vineyards is a historic Santa Cruz Mountains estate whose winemaking has been guided by Jeffrey Patterson since 1981, with a Burgundian, low-intervention approach. For this bottling they've sourced Chardonnay from the same Edna Valley planting since 1985 — vines planted in 1976 by local pioneer Andy MacGregor, in a vineyard owned by Jean Pierre Wolff since 1999. Cool Pacific air makes Edna Valley one of California's chilliest growing regions, so the wine keeps bright acid and stony freshness under its barrel-fermented texture.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It's the serious crossover Chardonnay — California richness with white-Burgundy poise from a legacy producer, perfect for the guest who 'doesn't do buttery Chard.'

bottles.name: Pierre Thibert Chorey-les-Beaune
bottles.profile: Textbook red Burgundy: raspberry and black cherry lifted by earth, forest floor, and gentle spice. Bright acidity and fine, subtle tannins make it lively and food-friendly.
bottles.tenSecond: Real red Burgundy without the Grand Cru price — fresh, earthy Pinot Noir; the friendly door into the Côte de Beaune.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid and silky, restrained tannin flatter lighter proteins and mushrooms; the savory earth tone mirrors umami while the acid keeps fat in check.
bottles.mnemonic: Chorey-les-Beaune = the humble neighbor of Aloxe-Corton; honest, lively Pinot at a gentler price.
bottles.producerStory: Pierre Thibert wasn't born into wine — he built his small family domaine in Corgoloin from scratch in 1989, and with his wife Aline now farms roughly ten acres of vines including Chorey-lès-Beaune, Nuits-Saint-Georges and Côte de Nuits villages. The work is traditional and detail-obsessed, with maturation in tank or used wood depending on the cuvée, and the domaine has a loyal French following with regular citations in guides like the Guide Hachette. His Chorey-lès-Beaune is honest, earthy village Burgundy from the flats below Aloxe-Corton.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It's the friendly door into real red Burgundy — an artisan grower's Pinot that delivers the forest-floor experience without a Grand Cru markup.

bottles.name: Raventós i Blanc de Nit Rosé
bottles.profile: Very pale salmon-pink, traditional-method bubbles with red apple, blood orange, white cherry and a saline, herb-edged snap. Dry (Extra Brut) with a fine, creamy mousse and a tiny grippy texture that makes it a proper food sparkler, not a sweet aperitif.
bottles.tenSecond: Dry Spanish sparkling rosé from the family that invented Cava — pale, saline, and built for oysters, crudo, and salty-fresh plates.
bottles.pairWhy: High acid plus fine bubbles scrub salt and fat off the palate, and the saline, faintly grippy character mirrors brine — so raw shellfish, crudo, and fried snacks taste cleaner and brighter with every sip.

pronunciation.say: Raventós i Blanc de Nit Rosé
pronunciation.respell: rah-ven-TOHS ee BLAHNK deh NEET roh-ZAY

bottles.mnemonic: 'de Nit' = 'of the night' — picked before dawn so the Monastrell tints it just barely pink.
bottles.producerStory: The Raventós family has grown vines on this Penedès estate since 1497, and ancestor Josep Raventós made Spain's first traditional-method sparkling wine in 1872 — effectively inventing Cava. In 2012 Raventós i Blanc famously walked away from the Cava DO to create the stricter Conca del Riu Anoia designation: estate fruit, native grapes, biodynamic farming and longer aging. De Nit is their pale rosé — the classic trio of Xarel·lo, Macabeu and Parellada tinted with a small dose of Monastrell, aged around 18 months on the lees.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It's the sparkling rosé with pedigree — bone-dry, saline and food-first from the family that invented Cava and then outgrew it, ideal for oysters and crudo.

bottles.name: Sandrine & Fabrice Gasnier Chinon Pierres Chaudes
bottles.profile: Raspberry, red currant, and cassis with graphite, garrigue herbs, and a touch of pepper. Silky tannins and fresh acidity give a medium-bodied, savory Loire Cabernet Franc.
bottles.tenSecond: Loire Cabernet Franc — bright red fruit with a leafy, peppery edge and smooth tannins. Great with herbs, charcuterie, and lamb.
bottles.pairWhy: Medium tannin and fresh acid handle herbs and gamey fat without turning harsh; the wine's own peppery, herbal streak echoes green and spiced flavors on the plate.

pronunciation.say: Sandrine & Fabrice Gasnier Chinon Pierres Chaudes

aliases: sandrine & fabrice chinon gasnier pierres chaudes
bottles.mnemonic: Chinon = the Loire's home of Cabernet Franc; 'Pierres Chaudes' = warm stones = riper, rounder fruit.
bottles.producerStory: Fabrice Gasnier is a fourth-generation grower in Cravant-les-Côteaux, the heart of Chinon, where he and his wife Sandrine farm around thirty hectares of mostly old-vine Cabernet Franc. The domaine has been biodynamic since 2008, certified by both Ecocert and Demeter. Les Pierres Chaudes ('warm stones') comes from clay-silica soils strewn with small stones over limestone — a sunny site that gives riper, rounder fruit while keeping Chinon's signature peppery, herbal edge.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It's the sommelier's mid-weight red — biodynamic Loire Cab Franc whose leafy, peppery savour flatters herbs, charcuterie and lamb in a way crowd-pleaser reds can't.

bottles.name: Terroir Sense Fronteres Negre de Montsant
bottles.profile: Crunchy cherry and wild berry with warm spice, a hint of licorice, and a mineral, stony finish. Fresh acidity and fine, silky tannins keep it savory rather than jammy.
bottles.tenSecond: Fresh, stony Grenache from Montsant — the step up from our by-the-glass Sindicat, great with sausage, lamb, and duck.
bottles.pairWhy: Medium body, medium acid, and supple tannins handle fat and spice without bullying the plate — acid cuts richness, gentle grip frames the meat.

pronunciation.say: Terroir Sense Fronteres Negre de Montsant
pronunciation.respell: teh-ROIR SEN-seh fron-TEH-res NEH-greh deh mon-SAHN

bottles.mnemonic: 'Sense Fronteres' = no borders; a fresher, lifted style of Garnacha (warm region, restrained winemaking) vs jammy Spanish reds.
bottles.producerStory: Terroir Sense Fronteres ('terroir without borders') is Dominik Huber's Montsant project, launched in 2016 as a sister to Terroir al Límit, the Priorat estate he co-founded with Eben Sadie in 2001 and has run solo since 2012. The approach is radically hands-off: organic farming, hand harvest, whole-bunch fermentation with wild yeasts, no oak — Negre is Garnatxa from vines around Capçanes at 300–350 metres, raised entirely in stainless steel. The result is Montsant with Priorat-adjacent minerality but fresher, lighter hands.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It's the fresh, stony Grenache that proves warm-climate Spain can be lifted and savory — the natural step up for anyone who loves our by-the-glass Garnacha.

bottles.name: Texier Brézème
bottles.profile: Red and black fruit, black olive, cured meat and cracked black pepper over a stony mineral core. Fresh, savoury and medium-bodied — northern Rhône Syrah in a peppery, almost Burgundian style, not a jammy bruiser.
bottles.tenSecond: The peppery, savoury Syrah — black olive, smoke and cracked pepper with real freshness, made for lamb, sausage and grilled meat.
bottles.pairWhy: Black-pepper and savoury olive notes echo grilled and charred meats, while the bright acidity and medium tannin keep up with fat without the wine tasting heavy or sweet.
bottles.mnemonic: Brézème = the lone northern-Rhône slope; cool, peppery Syrah.
bottles.producerStory: Éric Texier is a former nuclear engineer from Bordeaux who retrained in wine (including time with Jean-Marie Guffens in Burgundy) and became famous for resurrecting forgotten Rhône terroirs. His signature rescue is Brézème, a lone south-facing hill at the very southern tip of the northern Rhône that had 19th-century fame alongside Hermitage before nearly vanishing; Texier replanted and now farms most of his own vines there. His style is self-described old-school and minimalist — cool, peppery, savory Syrah rather than a jammy bruiser.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It's the savory Syrah slot — black pepper, olive and smoke with real freshness for the lamb and steak crowd, plus a great comeback story servers can actually tell.

bottles.name: White Rock
bottles.region: Napa Valley (Stags Leap foothills), California, USA
bottles.profile: Dark plum, blackberry and bramble with leather, old cedar, tobacco spice and roasted coffee. Full-bodied and concentrated from old-vine volcanic-ash soils, but balanced and refined rather than an over-ripe fruit bomb — the structured, age-worthy Napa Cabernet.
bottles.tenSecond: The serious estate Napa Cabernet — dark berry, cedar and coffee with firm tannin and real structure, the top steak red on the list.
bottles.pairWhy: Firm, full Cabernet tannin is built for the fattiest beef — ribeye and steak — binding protein and fat so both wine and meat taste smoother; the savoury cedar/tobacco notes echo the char.
bottles.mnemonic: White Rock = white volcanic ash soils at the foot of Stags Leap; structured Napa Cab.
bottles.producerStory: White Rock is one of Napa's 'ghost wineries' — established in 1870 by Dr. John Pettingill, who built the winery from white volcanic stone quarried on the property in the southern foothills of the Stags Leap range. Henri and Claire Vandendriessche bought and revived the estate in 1977, and their family still farms it, producing only around 3,000 cases a year of estate Cabernet Sauvignon, Claret and Chardonnay. The house style is classic and age-worthy rather than over-ripe — old-school Napa from volcanic-ash soils.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It's the top steak Cabernet on the list — a small family estate with 150 years of history, giving big-night guests structure and a story instead of just a famous label.

bottles.name: Whitehall Lane
bottles.profile: Ripe plum, red cherry and mixed berry with mocha, chocolate and a touch of vanilla and licorice. Full-bodied, supple and round with fine, creamy tannins — the soft, plush, crowd-pleasing Napa red.
bottles.tenSecond: The smooth, plush Napa Merlot — ripe plum, cherry and chocolate with soft tannin; an easy, generous red for almost any table.
bottles.pairWhy: Soft, supple tannin and ripe fruit make it gentle and flexible — it flatters grilled chicken, duck and medium-weight beef without the firm grip that can fight delicate dishes.
bottles.mnemonic: Merlot = soft, plush, plummy; Napa = ripe and full.
bottles.producerStory: Whitehall Lane Winery sits on a St. Helena site first planted to vines in the 1800s; the modern winery was founded in 1979 and bought in 1993 by the Leonardini family of San Francisco, who still run it today. The family built its reputation on Merlot and Cabernet, farming eight estate vineyards totalling more than 200 acres across St. Helena, Rutherford, Oak Knoll and beyond. Their Merlot is a long-running Napa benchmark for the plush, polished style.
bottles.whyWePourIt: It's the smooth crowd-pleaser among the structured reds — a family-grown Napa Merlot soft enough to flatter almost any table when a big Cab would be too much.

beers.name: 33 Acres Ocean Pale Ale
beers.flavor: Citrus and floral hop aroma anchored by classic pine, over light caramel malt; light amber, light-bodied and crisp.

beers.name: Banded Peak Approach Amber Lager
beers.flavor: Toasty Vienna and Munich malt with light caramel and hazelnut, balanced by Czech Saaz hops; smooth and easy-drinking.

beers.name: Banded Peak Microburst Hazy IPA
beers.flavor: Soft and hazy with vibrant tropical fruit — ripe mango, pineapple and citrus zest with subtle pine; juicy, smooth finish.

beers.name: Banded Peak Mount Crushmore Pilsner
beers.flavor: Grainy malt, light lemongrass and floral hop notes, finishing clean, dry and crisp.

beers.name: Born Arm Candy Milk Stout
beers.flavor: Creamy and smooth with cream-enriched dark chocolate, mocha coffee and roasted malt; lactose-rounded with a gentle dry finish.

beers.name: Brewsmith Signature Pub Ale
beers.flavor: Malt-forward and biscuity with toasty English specialty malts and gentle bitterness; easy, sessionable.

beers.name: Chimay Blue
beers.flavor: Rich and warming with dark fruit — plum, raisin and fig — plus peppery/nutmeg spice, bready roasted malt and a creamy depth; sip it, don't slam it.

beers.name: Dandy The Julia Peach Cobbler Sour
beers.flavor: Tastes like peach cobbler — fresh Okanagan peach with vanilla and cinnamon, generous tartness over a touch of malty sweetness.

beers.name: Establishment Afternoon Delight NEPA
beers.flavor: Silky and hazy with juicy tropical fruit from Citra and Cashmere hops over a biscuity malt base; soft, low-bitterness finish.

beers.name: Four Winds Nectarous Dry-Hopped Sour
beers.flavor: Bright nectarine, peach, passion fruit and citrus over a complex, tart-but-balanced acidity; crisp, clean finish.

beers.name: Michelob Ultra
beers.flavor: Very light-bodied, crisp and dry with subtle malt and almost no bitterness; clean and refreshing.

beers.name: Ol' Beautiful Okami Kasu Japanese Lager
beers.style: Japanese-style rice lager/ale (brewed with sake kasu)
beers.flavor: Light and silky from the rice, with steamed-rice and soft melon notes and a clean, dry, easy finish.

pronunciation.say: Ol' Beautiful Okami Kasu Japanese Lager

beers.name: Polyrhythm Matinee Lemon Cream Tart Ale
beers.flavor: Bright and tart, like liquid lemon meringue pie — lemon-cream tartness with a soft, creamy edge and no real bitterness.

beers.name: Stella Artois
beers.flavor: Clean and crisp with light malt sweetness and a gentle hop bitterness; dry, refreshing finish.

beers.name: Superflux Happyness IPA
beers.style: West Coast IPA (with New England / hazy character)
beers.flavor: Loaded with Mosaic hops — papaya, peach, grapefruit and candied orange with floral pine over a slightly sweet medium malt; pours a slightly hazy gold.

beers.name: Uncommon Tropical Cider
beers.flavor: Ripe kiwi aroma with pineapple, passion fruit and papaya and a soft coconut-water mouthfeel; fruity, dry-hopped with Citra/Zamba/Hallertau Blanc.

beers.name: Village Wit
beers.flavor: Soft unfiltered wheat with orange zest, coriander, and a light Belgian-yeast spice; creamy and crisp.

beers.name: Peroni Pilsner 0.0
beers.flavor: Crisp, dry, lightly bitter — a clean lager profile without the alcohol.

beers.name: Noughty Rouge
beers.flavor: Soft dark-berry fruit with light spice; like most de-alcoholized reds it reads slightly sweet — set expectations honestly.

beers.name: Freixenet Sparkling Wine
beers.flavor: Crisp apple-citrus bubbles — the zero-proof palate reset for salty and fried plates.

fortifieds.name: Amaro Montenegro
fortifieds.profile: A light, aromatic amaro from Bologna (created 1885 by Stanislao Cobianchi, 40 botanicals). More floral than most amari — orange peel, rose petal, lavender and vanilla over a gentle herbal bitterness. Low-proof (23%), soft and bittersweet, it's the most crowd-friendly digestif on the list: lovely neat over ice. House note: this is the amaro in the Spaghetti Western cocktail.

fortifieds.name: Averna
fortifieds.profile: A Sicilian amaro (1868 recipe by Salvatore Averna) and one of Italy's best known. Velvety and bittersweet: caramel and candied orange arrive first, sweetness coating the palate, then a gentle bitterness of herbs, citrus and roots follows. Smooth and approachable — a great gateway amaro and a mellow after-dinner sip. House note: this is the amaro in the Doctor Jones cocktail.

fortifieds.name: Barbeito Madeira Rainwater Reserva 5yr
fortifieds.profile: Light-gold Madeira with dried fruit, orange blossom, candied orange and roasted-nut notes; full and round on the palate with that signature tangy oxidative, mineral-fresh finish that keeps it lively rather than heavy.

fortifieds.name: Boulard XO Calvados
fortifieds.profile: Calvados is Normandy apple (cider) brandy. Boulard XO blends Pays d'Auge crus aged 6-15 years in oak. Bright amber, with apple tart, vanilla, oak and toasted almond on the nose; the palate is dry but velvety — ripe and candied apple, honey, caramel, roasted almond and gentle cinnamon spice, finishing long with ripe apple and spice. A warming after-dinner sipper — and a natural with the Apple Tatin.

fortifieds.name: Castarède XO Armagnac
fortifieds.profile: Armagnac is Gascon grape brandy, distilled in a continuous (column) still — richer and more rustic than cognac. Castarède (the world's oldest Armagnac house) ages this XO a minimum of ~20 years in oak. Coppery, with candied chestnut, dried currant, glazed ripe plum, cigar box, sandalwood, nutmeg and a hint of rancio over a long, smooth finish. A deep, spicy after-dinner sipper.

fortifieds.name: Christian Drouin XO Calvados
fortifieds.profile: A Pays d'Auge calvados from cider apples, double-distilled in copper stills and aged at least 6 years in a mix of ex-Bordeaux, ex-sherry and ex-cognac casks. Baked apple and tarte tatin on the nose moving to a warm mix of cinnamon-baked apple, almond, apricot, roasted nut, oak and raisin. Drier and more polished than a young calvados — a refined after-dinner pour, lovely with the Apple Tatin.

fortifieds.name: Château de Montifaud VS Cognac
fortifieds.profile: A grower/estate cognac from the Vallet family's Petite Champagne vineyards (a top cru), routinely aged beyond the legal minimum — their VS sits around 4-5 years (vs the 2-year minimum). Vine-blossom nose with sweet grape, fresh stone fruit, apple, vanilla and bright nutty oak. A cleaner, more delicate house cognac than the big négociant brands.

fortifieds.name: Château de Montifaud VSOP Cognac
fortifieds.profile: Montifaud's VSOP — the estate's best-seller — is aged about 8-10 years, well over the 4-year minimum. Brown sugar, vanilla, cocoa and hazelnut over lots of oak, with a long, drying clove-spiced finish. A more characterful, grower-style alternative to the big-house VSOPs.

fortifieds.name: Château de Montifaud XO Cognac
fortifieds.profile: Montifaud's XO is aged about 30 years — far beyond the 10-year minimum. Dried fruit, dark oak, toasted nuts, baking spice, toffee and baked apple, lifted by bright white-peach, honeysuckle and sweet-grape notes. A deep, complex grower XO and the top cognac pour on the list.

fortifieds.name: Darroze 12yr Armagnac
fortifieds.profile: Francis Darroze is a renowned Bas-Armagnac négociant who ages distillates from small growers. The 12-year 'Les Grands Assemblages' shows raisin, dried fruit and citrus zest (lemon, orange) with cinnamon, clove and licorice that bloom after a minute in the glass; the palate adds oak, grape and biscuit with almond and chocolate, finishing tannic and leathery with caramel and wood. A spicier, slightly higher-proof grape-brandy digestif than the cognacs.

fortifieds.name: Domaine Pouderoux Maury Vendange
fortifieds.type: vin doux naturel (Maury Grenat, fortified red)
fortifieds.profile: Deep garnet red, an early-bottled Maury bursting with sweet raspberry, blackberry and fresh dark cherry — fruity, warm and medium-full, with the fortified sweetness kept fresh by Grenache's dark-fruit lift.

fortifieds.name: Emilio Hidalgo Fino
fortifieds.profile: Bone-dry fino from 100% Palomino, aged in solera under a veil of flor — Hidalgo bottle theirs older than most (6-7 years vs the usual 2-3). Bready, yeasty nose with green olive, almond and a saline, bright-acid palate. Light-bodied and crisp — serve well-chilled. More an aperitif/start-of-meal pour than a sweet after-dinner digestif, but listed here in the sherry flight.

fortifieds.name: Emilio Hidalgo Oloroso Gobernador
fortifieds.profile: A dry (seco) oloroso from 100% Palomino — a short 2-3 yr biological start, then ~10 years oxidative with no flor, so it deepens to amber. Walnut, hazelnut, date cake and toasty smoke with a saline, long, balanced palate — only ~3 g/L sugar, so it tastes rich but finishes dry. Versatile: opens a meal or closes it as a digestif.

fortifieds.name: Fallentimber Honey Buck
fortifieds.profile: Light, lightly sweet honey with zesty fresh lemon and ginger; sparkling and refreshing, drinks more like a ginger cider or Moscow-mule cocktail than a beer.

fortifieds.name: Fernet Branca
fortifieds.profile: Amaro is a bitter Italian herbal liqueur. Fernet-Branca (1845 recipe, Milan) is the most intense, 'fernet' style — 27 herbs and spices including aloe, rhubarb and saffron, aged a year in oak. Bold menthol and eucalyptus, bitter herbs and roots, mint, black licorice and citrus peel. Very dry and bracing — the classic palate-resetting digestif (and the bartender's handshake).

fortifieds.name: Hennessy VS Cognac
fortifieds.profile: Cognac is grape brandy from the Cognac region, double-distilled in copper pot stills and oak-aged. VS ('Very Special') is the youngest tier, aged at least 2 years. Hennessy VS is bold and approachable — oak, vanilla and toasted almond with a light raisin, brown-sugar sweetness and floral lavender lift. The everyday house cognac: neat, on the rocks, or in cocktails.

fortifieds.name: Hennessy VSOP Cognac
fortifieds.type: cognac (VSOP — Very Superior Old Pale, min 4 years)
fortifieds.profile: VSOP ('Very Superior Old Pale') is aged at least 4 years — the middle tier, smoother and more refined than VS. Hennessy VSOP shows rich oak, vanilla and toasted almond with a hint of riper fruit and more polish. The classic balanced cognac for sipping neat after dinner.

fortifieds.name: Hennessy XO Cognac
fortifieds.profile: XO ('Extra Old') is aged at least 10 years (the legal minimum was raised from 6 to 10 years in 2018) — the rich, full-bodied prestige tier. Hennessy XO is complex and spicy: dark raisin and plum, orange peel and grapefruit, vanilla-laced milk chocolate, with a long finish of cocoa, cinnamon and barrel spice. Built for slow sipping neat — the cognac splurge on the list.

fortifieds.name: Kopke Late Bottled Vintage Port 2015
fortifieds.profile: A single-vintage (2015) ruby-style port from Kopke (the oldest Douro house, est. 1638), aged 4-6 years then bottled unfiltered. Deep dark-purple with ripe wild-berry, violet, black pepper and cacao; full-bodied, sweet, with fresh tannin and good acidity. Blend of Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Tinta Roriz and Sousão. Great after dinner on its own or with blue cheese and chocolate.

fortifieds.name: Marolo Milla Camomilla
fortifieds.profile: Grappa is Italian pomace brandy (distilled from grape skins). Marolo's 'Milla' is a liqueur made by steeping chamomile flowers for ~11 months in Marolo's Langhe grappa (distilled from Nebbiolo — the Barolo/Barbaresco grape — pomace). Floral, honeyed chamomile-tea aromas with peach-apricot and a light, smooth, delicate palate at 35%. Best served chilled or near-frozen — a soft, soothing way to close a meal.

fortifieds.name: Nonino
fortifieds.profile: An amaro from the Nonino grappa house in Friuli (Percoto), unusual for being built on the family's own grape distillate (with brandy) rather than plain neutral spirit, then infused with herbs, citrus and barrel-aged. Bittersweet caramel, vanilla and bitter orange up front, licorice, spice and dried herbs beneath, with a lingering cocoa finish. Smoother and more elegant than most amari — a refined after-dinner sipper.

fortifieds.name: Quevedo Tawny 10yr
fortifieds.profile: A 10-year-old tawny from Quevedo (a small São João da Pesqueira producer), oak-aged in small casks to an amber-tawny hue. Dried fig, toasted walnut, cinnamon and orange peel on the nose; silky palate of roasted nuts, coffee and dark chocolate wrapped in balanced sweetness, with a long caramelised-almond finish. The nutty, barrel-aged style of port — softer and more mellow than a ruby/LBV.

fortifieds.name: Taylor Fladgate Tawny 40yr
fortifieds.profile: Taylor Fladgate's 40-year-old tawny — decades of cask-aging concentrate it into dried fruit, honey, nutmeg, roasted coffee and intense nuttiness, in an old olive-gold hue. The entry is rich and almost viscous (date, dried fig, candied citrus) but gripping acidity keeps it from feeling heavy, with an extraordinarily long almond-and-spice finish. This is the splurge after-dinner pour on the list.

fortifieds.name: Valdespino Cream Sherry Isabela
fortifieds.profile: Mahogany-coloured and rich but not cloying — raisin, date, dried fig, candied orange, toffee pudding, and roasted walnut, with a long nutty finish that dries out slightly at the end.

fortifieds.name: Valdespino Single Vineyard Amontillado Tio Diego
fortifieds.profile: A dry amontillado from Valdespino's single Macharnudo Alto vineyard (sibling of the Inocente fino — same must). Roughly a decade under flor, then re-fortified to ~18% when the flor dies and it finishes oxidatively; around 18 years average age. Dry and austere with roasted hazelnut and almond, caramel, dried fig and toasted-oak spice, and notably high acidity. A serious, savoury sipping sherry — neat, lightly chilled.

pronunciation.say: Valdespino Single Vineyard Amontillado Tio Diego
